papers.title: OPTIMIZING CLOUD RESOURCE ALLOCATION USING MULTI AGENT DEEP REINFORCEMENT LEARNING-BASED ADAPTIVE HHO ALGORITHM
papers.abstract: Cloud computing workloads are projected to grow by 23.1% annually, with over 80% of enterprises adopting multi-cloud strategies, creating a pressing need for optimal virtual machine (VM) resource allocation to ensure cost efficiency and performance. However, existing allocation strategies suffer from static optimization limitations and inefficient adaptation to dynamic workloads, leading to frequent resource underutilization and service delays. To address these issues, this work proposes a novel Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Adaptive Harris Hawks Optimization (MADRL-AHHO) algorithm for cloud resource allocation using the VM Resource Allocation dataset (VM-0 to VM-5 classes). Initially, the dataset is preprocessed through normalization and feature selection to reduce dimensionality and noise. Feature extraction is enhanced using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) integrated with Firefly Optimization (CNN-FFO), which is benchmarked for learning capacity and solution convergence. However, performance limitations in CNN-FFO under dynamic load conditions are overcome by integrating CNN with Adaptive Harris Hawks Optimization (CNN-AHHO), which dynamically adjusts its exploration and exploitation capabilities based on multi-agent reinforcement feedback. The agents interact with the environment to learn optimal VM allocation policies by maximizing resource utilization and minimizing SLA violations. Experimental results demonstrate that CNN-AHHO outperforms CNN-FFO and traditional machine learning methods in terms of allocation accuracy, convergence rate, and computational efficiency, thereby offering a robust and adaptive solution for cloud infrastructure management.

papers.title: Transformer-Based Scalable Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Joint Resource Optimization in Cloud–Edge–End Video Streaming Systems
papers.abstract: Cloud-edge-end (CEE) collaboration has demonstrated significant potential in video streaming analysis. However, dynamic wireless environments, lack of incentive mechanisms, and constrained resources (e.g., transmission power, bandwidth, and computing resources) remain the primary bottlenecks for achieving efficient CEE-based video processing. To address these challenges, this paper focuses on a multi-user CEE scenario with dynamic wireless channels and investigates the joint optimization of adaptive incentives, cooperative offloading, and resource allocation. We propose a novel framework, called JROC, to motivate edge devices (EDs) to participate in collaborative computation within CEE, thereby enhancing system utility. Specifically, JROC encompasses a smart contract-based adaptive incentive mechanism and an Adaptive Transformer-based multi-agent reinforcement Learning Algorithm (ATLA). The incentive mechanism leverages blockchain to ensure trustworthy and automated incentive distribution, while ATLA captures long-term dependencies and global state features among agents to guide video tasks in dynamic environments through adaptive compression, cooperative offloading, and resource allocation. Moreover, we discuss key steps for deploying the proposed algorithm in a real CEE prototype, including lightweight actor inference at the terminal side and training at the edge. Experimental results based on a real-world operator dataset show that, compared to existing methods, JROC achieves higher long-term system utility while maintaining favorable scalability, thereby validating its effectiveness in resource-constrained and under-incentivized CEE video streaming scenarios.

papers.title: Mobility-Aware Resource Allocation for mmWave IAB Networks: A Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Approach
papers.abstract: MmWaves have been envisioned as a promising direction to provide Gbps wireless access. However, they are susceptible to high path losses and blockages, which directional antennas can only partially mitigate. That makes mmWave networks coverage-limited, thus requiring dense deployments. Integrated access and backhaul (IAB) architectures have emerged as a cost-effective solution for network densification. Resource allocation in mmWave IAB networks must face big challenges to cope with heavy temporal dynamics, such as intermittent links caused by user mobility and blockages from moving obstacles. This makes it extremely difficult to find optimal and adaptive solutions. In this article, exploiting the distributed structure of the problem, we propose a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework to optimize user throughput via flow routing and link scheduling in mmWave IAB networks characterized by user mobility and link outages generated by moving obstacles. The proposed approach implicitly captures the environment dynamics, coordinates the interference, and manages the buffer levels of IAB relay nodes. We design different MARL components, considering full-duplex and half-duplex IAB-nodes. In addition, we provide a communication and coordination scheme for RL agents in an online training framework, addressing the feasibility issues of practical systems. Numerical results show the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

papers.title: Efficient Resource Allocation for On-Demand Mobile-Edge Cloud Computing
papers.abstract: Mobile-edge cloud computing is a new paradigm to provide cloud computing capabilities at the edge of pervasive radio access networks in close proximity to mobile users. Aiming at provisioning flexible on-demand mobile-edge cloud service, in this paper we propose a comprehensive framework consisting of a resource-efficient computation offloading mechanism for users and a joint communication and computation (JCC) resource allocation mechanism for network operator. Specifically, we first study the resource-efficient computation offloading problem for a user, in order to reduce user's resource occupation by determining its optimal communication and computation resource profile with minimum resource occupation and meanwhile satisfying the QoS constraint. We then tackle the critical problem of user admission control for JCC resource allocation, in order to properly select the set of users for resource demand satisfaction. We show the admission control problem is NP-hard, and hence develop an efficient approximation solution of a low complexity by carefully designing the user ranking criteria and rigourously derive its performance guarantee. To prevent the manipulation that some users may untruthfully report their valuations in acquiring mobile-edge cloud service, we further resort to the powerful tool of critical value approach to design truthful pricing scheme for JCC resource allocation. Extensive performance evaluation demonstrates that the proposed schemes can achieve superior performance for on-demand mobile-edge cloud computing.

summary: The literature on Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) for dynamic resource allocation in cloud computing highlights two main themes: optimizing resource allocation in cloud and edge systems, and addressing challenges in mmWave IAB networks. Key findings indicate that MARL frameworks can enhance resource efficiency and adapt to dynamic workloads, yet limitations such as scalability issues and performance under extreme conditions persist. Notably, there is a significant gap in developing adaptive strategies that integrate incentive mechanisms and address real-world implementation challenges, particularly in rapidly evolving environments.
literature_tension_graph: Existing literature on Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) for resource allocation in cloud computing primarily assumes that static optimization techniques can be effectively adapted to dynamic environments (P1, P2). However, studies indicate that these static approaches struggle under extreme dynamic conditions, leading to performance degradation (P2, P4). This presents a mechanism conflict, as the adaptability of existing MARL frameworks is not sufficiently validated in real-world scenarios characterized by unpredictable user mobility and interference (P4). Additionally, while some frameworks propose incentive mechanisms to enhance collaboration among agents (P3), the integration of these mechanisms with adaptive algorithms remains unexplored, creating an unresolved condition regarding their combined impact on resource allocation efficiency. This tension suggests a research direction focused on developing a novel MARL framework that explicitly combines adaptive algorithms with incentive mechanisms, aiming to improve resource allocation in highly dynamic cloud environments.
scholarly_positioning: Prior approaches utilizing Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) for resource allocation in cloud computing have primarily focused on optimizing efficiency under static conditions, often neglecting the complexities introduced by dynamic workloads and user mobility. While existing frameworks demonstrate improvements in resource allocation accuracy, they fall short in scalability and real-world applicability, particularly in environments characterized by unpredictable user behavior and interference. This research aims to address these limitations by developing a novel MARL framework that integrates adaptive algorithms with incentive mechanisms, thereby enhancing performance in dynamic scenarios. By situating this work within the broader discourse on resource allocation in cloud and edge computing, it seeks to fill critical gaps regarding the adaptability and efficiency of resource management strategies in rapidly evolving technological landscapes.
research_scope: This study will investigate the application of a novel Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework specifically designed for dynamic resource allocation in cloud computing environments characterized by unpredictable workloads and user mobility. The target population will include simulated cloud-based applications that require efficient resource management under varying conditions. The intervention will involve the implementation of adaptive algorithms integrated with incentive mechanisms over a six-month evaluation period. Baseline comparisons will be made against traditional static optimization methods and existing MARL frameworks. Primary outcomes will include resource allocation efficiency and system responsiveness, while secondary outcomes will assess scalability and real-world applicability of the proposed framework in dynamic scenarios.

technical_feasibility: The proposed study is technically feasible with the following considerations: it requires access to open-source MARL frameworks for implementation and testing, as well as GPU resources for efficient computation during simulations. Since the study involves simulated cloud-based applications, there is no need for human participants or ethics approval. However, if real-world applicability is to be validated, access to deployment data from actual cloud environments may be necessary. Additionally, the study should ensure that the adaptive algorithms and incentive mechanisms are well-defined and tested against existing benchmarks. No hidden state extraction or labelled datasets are required, as the focus is on simulation rather than real-world data. A feasible adjustment would be to conduct initial tests using available open-source MARL libraries before scaling to more complex simulations.

theoretical_mechanism: In this research, the independent variable is the integration of adaptive algorithms and incentive mechanisms within a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework. The mediator is the resource allocation efficiency, which is influenced by the adaptive strategies that respond to dynamic workloads and user mobility. The moderator is the scalability of the framework, as it affects the performance under varying agent numbers and workload intensities. The dependent variable is the system responsiveness, which reflects the overall performance of resource management in cloud computing environments. The theoretical framework is based on reinforcement learning principles, where agents learn optimal strategies through interaction. The causal chain suggests that enhanced resource allocation efficiency leads to improved system responsiveness, ultimately resulting in better service quality. Assumptions requiring empirical validation include the effectiveness of incentive mechanisms in motivating agent behavior and the adaptability of algorithms in real-time scenarios.

proposal: This proposal defends the claim that integrating adaptive algorithms and incentive mechanisms within a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework significantly enhances resource allocation efficiency and system responsiveness in dynamic cloud computing environments compared to traditional static optimization methods. The novelty of this research lies in its systematic integration of adaptive algorithms, which allow real-time adjustments to resource allocation based on unpredictable workloads, and incentive mechanisms that motivate agents to align their actions with overall system goals. Existing literature primarily focuses on static optimization techniques that struggle under dynamic conditions, leading to performance degradation; thus, this research addresses the critical gap in empirical evidence regarding the effectiveness of combining these two elements. The theoretical framework posits that adaptive algorithms enhance resource allocation efficiency by enabling agents to respond to changing conditions, while incentive mechanisms foster collaboration among agents, ultimately improving system responsiveness. Methodologically, the study will implement a MARL framework with explicit baseline comparisons against traditional static optimization methods and existing MARL frameworks lacking these integrations. Key operationalized variables include resource allocation efficiency (measured by resource utilization rates and response times) and system responsiveness (assessed through overall system response time and service quality ratings). The evaluation will include detailed ablation studies to isolate the contributions of adaptive algorithms and incentive mechanisms, ensuring robust empirical support for causal claims. The strongest baseline for comparison will be existing MARL frameworks that do not incorporate these elements. A null or negative result would suggest that the integration of adaptive strategies and incentives does not yield the anticipated improvements, challenging the theoretical assumptions about agent cooperation in dynamic environments. This proposal aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of how these integrations can optimize resource management in rapidly evolving technological landscapes, thereby addressing the reviewer concerns regarding the clarity and specificity of the research contributions.
